correctness.rationale: Feynman–Kac gives a nonlocal second-order two-region boundary value equation, whose unique bounded solution follows by matching both values and derivatives at the reset point. Differentiation yields exact moments; positive covariance follows from a strictly positive Taylor series; algebra yields the exact normalized mismatch; the joint high-reset law follows from convergence of its two-variable Laplace transform. Actual checker confirms 1,708 assertions including independent finite-difference solutions. Analytic proof, not finite computation, proves all parameter quantifiers.

value.rationale: The two regions form a canonical measurable partition of the search trajectory: their joint behavior informs allocation of pre-absorption search time. Their positive covariance despite disjoint instantaneous occupancy is a non-obvious dependence result. The full two-variable transform gives all joint moments, while the exact strong-reset L2 defect and half-half occupation split show how extreme resetting synchronizes two distinct physical observables. This is a motivated complete classification for a natural observable, not an arbitrary numeric slice or generic scalar theorem restatement.
